title: Cost of Government study of housing approvals
summary: On August 13, the commission voted five to one to create a temporary investigative group on housing policies and the approvals process; one member was excused and one recused because they work as a planner. A commissioner called permitting key to building more affordable and workforce housing, citing reports that permits can take 300 to 400 days. The commission's lawyer urged studying all approvals, including subdivisions, and a kickoff meeting with the mayor's office, council and departments is wanted.

timeline.text: The motion to create the study group passed with five ayes and one nay.
Motion to establish a temporary investigative group on housing policies and the approvals process: The motion passed with five ayes and one nay; one member was excused and one recused.
The commission voted five to one to create a Temporary Investigative Group (TIG) on housing policies and the approvals process.
The commissioner wants a kickoff meeting with the mayor's office, the council and departments to find a contact person at each.
One commissioner recused, or stepped out of the vote, because they work as a planner.
The commission's lawyer suggested studying all approvals, not just permits, because things like subdivision approvals also matter.
The commissioner said they had heard permits can take up to 300 to 400 days.
A commissioner said the permitting process is a key part of building more housing, especially affordable and workforce housing.
